test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 1) Foundational Full Test - 02
subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements regarding the President of India:

1. In the case of the pregnancy of a woman offender, he may completely absolve her guilt using Respite power.

2. He does not act as a court of appeal while using his pardoning powers.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2 only.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Judicial Powers of the President of India:**

 
 
• The President appoints the Chief Justice & other Judges of the S.C & H.C.
 
• Under Article 143, he can seek advice from S.C on any question of law.
 
 
• The advice tendered by S.C is not binding on the President.
 
 
 
• Article 72 confers the President power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment or to commute the sentence of any person convicted of an offence.
 
 
• **Pardoning powers of the President include**:
 
 
• **Pardon:** Completely absolves the guilt of the offender.
 
• **Reprieve:** It refers to the temporary stay on the death sentence or life imprisonment.
 
• **Respite:** It refers to the awarding a lesser sentence on a special ground like the pregnancy of a woman offender.
 
 
• **Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.**
 
 
 
• **Remission:** Reducing the amount of sentence without changing the nature of punishment.
 
• **Commutation: **Changing one punishment to another form from a death sentence to life imprisonment.
 
 
 
 
 
• S.C has laid down certain principles regarding the pardoning power of the President:
 
 
• The petitioner has no right to an oral hearing by the President.
 
• The President can examine the evidence afresh taking a view different from the courts.
 
• President exercises this power on the advice of the Union Cabinet.
 
 
 
• The President while using this power, does not act as a court of appeal.
 
 
• **Hence, statement 2 is correct.**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The pardoning power of the President is not subject to Judicial review except for those decisions which are arbitrary, irrational or discriminating.
 
• If one petition is rejected, stay can't be obtained by filing another petition on the same subject.
